listBibl.bibl: Felix Liebermann, Die Gesetze der Angelsachsen, vol. 1 (Halle: Niemeyer, 1903), p. 625

An English crib of the Latin text, semi-literal, made for this database in 2026 with Claude, a large language model (LLM) made by Anthropic. It keeps close to the wording of the original and uses the established English of Anglo-Latin legal, liturgical and canon-law formulae. It is an aid to reading the original, not a published translation. Square brackets mark Liebermann’s additions to the text or, now and then, words supplied for the sense; “[?]” marks a doubtful reading

div.head: Ps Cn for 27.1
div.ab: Sunt et alia quamplurima animalia, que, quanquam infra septa foreste uiuunt et oneri et curo mediocrium subiacent, foreste tamen nequaquam censeri possunt, qualia sunt equi, bubali, uacce et similia.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 625 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page); Liebermann’s print has ‘curo’ (for ‘cure’, i.e. curae); transcribed as printed
div.ab: There are also very many other animals which, although they live within the enclosures of the forest and are subject to the charge and care of the middling men, can nevertheless by no means be reckoned [beasts] of the forest, such as horses, buffaloes, cows and the like.
